name: Gothic academia

lead: Gothic academia is a variant of dark academia, the internet aesthetic built around universities, literature and the arts. It leans on the gothic side: darker palettes, Gothic architecture and a melancholic, romantic mood.

For someone's looks, it is a clothing and presentation style: tailored layers in black, brown, beige and dark green that give a studious, brooding appearance. It is cheap to assemble from thrifted pieces.

paras: Wearers combine blazers, cardigans, dress shirts, tweed or houndstooth, plaid and Oxford shoes in muted dark colours, often sourced second-hand. Accessories, books and autumn imagery reinforce the look.
No physical risks. Commentators criticise the wider aesthetic as elitist and for glamorising overwork and substance misuse.

angle.text: Gothic academia gives a coordinated wardrobe direction: dark tailored layers, knitwear and classic shoes. Wearers use it to look studious and moody.

lead: Gothic academia is one of the offshoots of dark academia, an internet aesthetic centred on higher education, the arts and literature.[1] Dark academia emerged on Tumblr around 2014-2015, gained prominence on Instagram and Pinterest around 2017 and expanded in the early 2020s through TikTok.[1] Donna Tartt's 1992 novel The Secret History is widely credited as its inspiration.[1]

The look draws on 1930s-1940s collegiate fashion associated with Oxbridge, Ivy League and prep schools: cardigans, blazers, dress shirts, plaid skirts, Oxford shoes and tweed or houndstooth, in black, white, beige, brown and dark green.[1] Gothic and Collegiate Gothic architecture is central to the imagery, and like goth subculture the style romanticises beauty in dark themes.[1] Gothic academia is listed among the offshoots alongside chaotic, green and light academia.[1]

People use the style to shape how they present themselves, with thrift stores a common source of clothing, which some see as more accessible than related trends.[1] Critics call the aesthetic Eurocentric and elitist, and fault it for glamorising overwork and substance misuse.[1]

paras: Dark academia centres on idealised campus life, with clothing from mid-century collegiate fashion and interiors of dark wood, candlelight and libraries.[1] The gothic variant emphasises the melancholic and architectural side of this mood.[1]

The aesthetic spread from Tumblr to Instagram and Pinterest and then TikTok, especially during pandemic-era school closures.[1] Source works include The Picture of Dorian Gray and films such as Dead Poets Society, and the 1965 book Take Ivy is described as an early codification of parts of the look.[1]

Commentators describe the aesthetic as reliant on a largely white literary canon and as an 'old money' look tied to elite education.[1] Others read it as a reaction to the corporatisation of higher education.[1]

timeline.event: Donna Tartt publishes The Secret History, widely credited as a source.[1]
Dark academia begins to emerge on Tumblr.[1]
The aesthetic gains prominence on Instagram and Pinterest.[1]
